subtitle: When the Kaveri Learned to Carry Light

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Shivanasamudra falls with faint transmission lines stretching toward a distant city
panels.action: K. Seshadri Iyer stands firm on a rocky ledge near the roaring Shivanasamudra falls while the young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, in simple regal dress, looks out toward the horizon where faint poles and wires vanish into mist.

dialogue.text: In Mysore’s twilight of princes and steam, K. Seshadri Iyer and a boy-king dared to ask: can the rage of the Kaveri carry light to far-off mines and a sleeping city?

i18n.hi: मैसूर के राजाओं और भाप के साँझ में, के. शेषाद्रि अय्यर और एक बाल–राजा ने पूछा: क्या गर्जती कावेरी दूर की खानों और सोती नगरी तक रोशनी पहुँचा सकती है?

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Mysore countryside with distant palace and British cantonment
panels.action: A panoramic view shows the Mysore palace domes rising over a modest town, beyond which lie a British cantonment and distant low hills, with bullock carts creaking along dusty roads under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: The year is 1898. Mysore is called a ‘model state’ by British officials, yet its nights glow only with oil lamps and its wealth lies hidden in deep, dark rock.

i18n.hi: साल 1898 है। अंग्रेज मैसूर को ‘मॉडल स्टेट’ कहते हैं, पर रातों में बस तेल के दीये हैं, और दौलत दबी है काले, गहरे पत्थरों में।

panels.shot: underground cross-section view, slightly low-angle, of miners in Kolar Gold Fields
panels.action: Deep underground in the Kolar Gold Fields, Indian miners in lamps and simple gear work by dim, flickering light, timber supports looming as shadowy shafts recede into darkness.

dialogue.text: At Kolar Gold Fields, British companies hunger for more ore, more speed, more profit. The mines need power—vast, steady, cheap. Steam engines gulp coal; the costs choke the venture.

i18n.hi: कोलार गोल्ड फील्ड्स में अंग्रेज कंपनियाँ और अय्यर चाहती हैं – ज़्यादा अयस्क, ज़्यादा रफ़्तार, ज़्यादा मुनाफ़ा। खानों को चाहिये ताक़त – भारी, टिकाऊ, सस्ती। भाप इंजन कोयला निगलते हैं; खर्चा गला घोंट देता है।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot in the Mysore durbar hall, slight low-angle on Seshadri Iyer addressing the regency council with the young prince present
panels.action: In the high-pillared durbar hall, K. Seshadri Iyer, in formal coat and turban, stands with papers in hand before a seated regency council; the young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV listens intently beside his guardian.

dialogue.text: Under Dewan Seshadri Iyer, the regency rules for the minor Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV. The Dewan sees in Kolar’s hunger a chance to remake Mysore with a new kind of power.

i18n.hi: दीवान शेषाद्रि अय्यर की हुकूमत में नाबालिग कृष्णराज वाडेयार चतुर्थ के नाम पर राज चलता है। दीवान को कोलार की भूख में मैसूर को नई ताक़त से गढ़ने का मौका दिखता है।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Seshadri Iyer presenting a map, with the young prince in profile
panels.action: Seshadri Iyer leans over a large map spread on a polished table, his finger tracing from Shivanasamudra Falls to Kolar, while the young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV watches, eyes bright with curiosity.

dialogue.speaker: K. Seshadri Iyer & Young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
dialogue.text: “We will make the Kaveri climb hills and cross plains as light.”

i18n.hi: “हम कावेरी को पहाड़ चढ़ाकर, मैदान पार कर, रोशनी बना देंगे।”

panels.shot: wide shot at Shivanasamudra, slightly high-angle, showing surveyors at work
panels.action: On the rocky banks of Shivanasamudra, Seshadri Iyer stands with British and Indian engineers as surveyors sight along tripods; behind them the split Kaveri crashes in white torrents around lush islands.

dialogue.text: They choose Shivanasamudra, where the Kaveri breaks into furious falls. Here, gravity itself can drive great turbines. But no one in India has yet sent such power so far.

i18n.hi: वे चुनते हैं शिवनसमुद्र, जहाँ कावेरी पागल धाराओं में टूट पड़ती है। यहाँ खुद गुरुत्वाकर्षण विशाल टर्बाइन घुमा सकता है। मगर हिंदुस्तान में किसी ने इतनी दूर तक इतनी ताक़त भेज ही नहीं।

panels.shot: interior workshop mid-shot, with engineers poring over blueprints and alternator designs
panels.action: In a cluttered room, Indian draughtsmen and European engineers bend over blueprints of dynamos and turbines, compasses and slide rules scattered among ink-stained papers.

dialogue.text: Alternating current is still new, argued over in Europe and America. Mysore’s officials weigh risks: can fragile wires carry this invisible force sixty, seventy miles without failing?

i18n.hi: आल्टरनेटिंग करंट अभी नया है, यूरोप–अमेरिका में बहस जारी है। मैसूर के अफ़सर तौलते हैं: क्या नाज़ुक तार ये अदृश्य ताक़त साठ–सत्तर मील तक उठा ले जाएँगे?

panels.shot: small council-room shot, mid-level, Dewan in debate with a British official while the young prince listens quietly
panels.action: In a smaller council chamber, Seshadri Iyer sits upright opposite a British resident and mine representative, while the young prince listens from a side chair, hands folded, absorbing every word.

dialogue.text: Mysore will bear the cost; the company will buy the power. Imperial gazetteers later note this quiet bargain: a princely state funding modern works, not merely paying tribute.

i18n.hi: खर्चा मैसूर उठाएगा, कंपनी बिजली खरीदेगी। साम्राज्य के गज़ेटियर बाद में इस खामोश सौदे को दर्ज करेंगे: एक रियासत जो टैक्स नहीं, तरक़्क़ी पर पैसा बहाती है।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of construction at Shivanasamudra, with scaffolding and masonry in the spray of the falls
panels.action: Workers in dhotis and turbans haul stone and steel across scaffolds clinging to the wet rock, as a half-built powerhouse takes shape under the mist of the falling Kaveri.

dialogue.text: Through the late 1890s, stone by stone, coil by coil, the powerhouse rises. Turbines from abroad meet local craft; Mysore’s own lines department grows around this roaring classroom.

i18n.hi: पूरे 1890 के दशक में, पत्थर पर पत्थर, कुंडली पर कुंडली, पावरहाउस खड़ा होता है। बाहर से आए टर्बाइन लोकल हुनर से मिलते हैं; मैसूर का बिजली विभाग इसी गरजती क्लासरूम के इर्द–गिर्द बनता है।

panels.shot: interior of the completed powerhouse, wide shot, with massive generators and engineers in place
panels.action: Inside the completed powerhouse, gleaming turbines and large generators sit on solid foundations, Indian engineers in neatly pressed coats standing ready beside control panels and gauges.

dialogue.text: By 1902, the scheme stands ready. Government reports will soon record a new phrase in Mysore’s ledgers: ‘Shivanasamudra hydroelectric station, supplying Kolar Gold Fields.’

i18n.hi: 1902 तक योजना तैयार खड़ी है। सरकारी रिपोर्टों में जल्द ही नया जुमला दर्ज होता है: ‘शिवनसमुद्र जलविद्युत केंद्र, सप्लाइंग कोलार गोल्ड फील्ड्स।’

panels.shot: symbolic close-up of Seshadri Iyer’s hand on a control lever, with the prince watching in the background
panels.action: Seshadri Iyer’s steady hand rests on a large switch lever in the powerhouse as the young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV stands just behind him, face tense with anticipation.

dialogue.speaker: K. Seshadri Iyer & Young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
dialogue.text: “From this fall, may all Mysore be lit.”

i18n.hi: “इस गिर तक से, पूरा मैसूर जगमगाए।”

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot showing the turbines beginning to spin and lights flickering on in the station
panels.action: The mighty turbines blur into motion, spray rising higher, while lamps along the interior walls of the station spring to bright, steady life.

dialogue.text: The switch falls. Water drives steel; steel drives copper. Invisible currents hum into the long lines that run over hills and dry tank-beds toward the buried gold.

i18n.hi: स्विच गिरता है। पानी इस्पात को घुमाता है; इस्पात ताँबे को। अदृश्य धाराएँ पहाड़ियों और सूखे टैंकों के ऊपर दौड़ती लंबी तारों में गुनगुनाती हैं, दबी सोने की तरफ़।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye following transmission lines across countryside toward Kolar
panels.action: From high above, thin transmission lines stride on tall poles across fields, streams, and scrubland, threading toward the distant cluster of Kolar’s mine headframes.

dialogue.text: Across sixty miles, the lines carry alternating current at high voltage—among Asia’s earliest such journeys of power from river to distant industry.

i18n.hi: साठ मील से ज़्यादा, ये तार ऊँचे वोल्ट पर आल्टरनेटिंग करंट ढोते हैं—एशिया में नदी से दूर उद्योग तक ताक़त की शुरुआती यात्राओं में से एक।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a KGF surface workshed as electric motors start up
panels.action: Inside a large shed at Kolar, belts on new electric motors jerk, then whirl smoothly, as idle machines shudder to life and miners watch with cautious wonder.

dialogue.text: At Kolar, motors turn without steam boilers, cages rise with new speed, and the deep levels glow brighter. The mine books show it plainly: costs fall, output climbs.

i18n.hi: कोलार में अब मोटरें बिना भाप बॉयलरों के घूमती हैं, पिंजरे नई रफ़्तार से ऊपर आते हैं, गहरे स्तर और चमक उठते हैं। खान की किताबें साफ़ दिखाती हैं: खर्चा गिरा, उत्पादन चढ़ा।

panels.shot: soft-lit interior of the Mysore palace study, mid-shot of the now slightly older prince reading a report with Seshadri Iyer nearby
panels.action: In a quiet palace study some years later, a slightly older Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV reads a bound report by lamplight, while an aging Seshadri Iyer, seated nearby, watches with tired satisfaction.

dialogue.text: Dewan Seshadri Iyer does not live to see every fruit of this work, yet the young king grows into his role with these reports as his early scriptures of governance.

i18n.hi: दीवान शेषाद्रि अय्यर इस मेहनत के हर फल को देख नहीं पाते, पर युवा राजा इन्हीं रिपोर्टों को अपने राजकाज के शुरुआती धर्मग्रंथ की तरह पढ़ते हुए बड़ा होता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bangalore’s South Parade (MG Road area) at dusk, with the young Maharaja and officials inspecting new street lamp posts
panels.action: On a broad Bangalore street at dusk around 1905, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, now in full regal dress, strolls with officials between tall iron lamp posts, while British and Indian townspeople gather expectantly.

dialogue.text: From Shivanasamudra, spare capacity and new lines now reach Bangalore. Mysore’s capital prepares to trade its smoky lamps for arcs of electric brightness along its main roads.

i18n.hi: शिवनसमुद्र से अब बची हुई बिजली और नई लाइनें बैंगलोर तक पहुँचती हैं। मैसूर की राजधानी तय करती है कि धुएँदार दीयों की जगह मुख्य सड़कों पर बिजली की चकाचौंध लेगी।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle wide of the first electric street lamps flaring to life over Bangalore’s street
panels.action: As the sky darkens, a row of tall street lamps suddenly flare with harsh white light above the street, illuminating the faces of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, officials, and onlookers in sharp relief.

dialogue.text: When the current is released, a rush of light runs down the line. Bangalore’s streets blaze with a new, steady glare—reportedly among the earliest electric street lighting in Asia.

i18n.hi: जैसे ही करंट छोड़ा जाता है, रोशनी की लहर तारों में दौड़ पड़ती है। बैंगलोर की गलियाँ नई, ठहरी हुई चमक में जल उठती हैं—कहा जाता है, एशिया की शुरुआती इलेक्ट्रिक स्ट्रीट लाइटिंग में से एक।

panels.shot: gentle mid-shot of the Maharaja looking up at the lights, with a portrait of Seshadri Iyer in the background
panels.action: In a government building, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV stands by a window looking out at the glowing street, while behind him on the wall hangs a framed portrait of K. Seshadri Iyer.

dialogue.speaker: K. Seshadri Iyer & Young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
dialogue.text: “Power must not end at the mine; it must reach the citizen.”

i18n.hi: “ताक़त खान पर खत्म नहीं होनी चाहिये; उसे नागरिक तक पहुँचना है।”

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of Mysore State maps and later works, dissolving from falls to gridlines
panels.action: A composite image shows the Shivanasamudra falls, then overlays of expanding transmission lines radiating across a map of Mysore, fading into glimpses of later dams and city lights.

dialogue.text: From this first cascade of wires grew Mysore’s wider grid, the later dams of Visvesvaraya’s age, and a new idea of rule: that a state’s glory lies in how far it carries light.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं पहली तारों के झरने से मैसूर का बड़ा ग्रिड उगा, विश्वेश्वरैया के दौर के बाँध बने, और राज चलाने का नया ख़याल जन्मा: कि रियासत की शान इस बात में है कि उसकी रोशनी कितनी दूर तक जाती है।
